R-0391.next: Expect "why were units used early?" — justification attached.

info.asked: Please provide additional clinical information to support medical necessity: (1) frequency and duration of physical aggression within the last 30 days; (2) documentation of prior outpatient treatment and outcome; (3) current IEP supports and why they are insufficient.
items: Frequency and duration of physical aggression within the last 30 days
Current IEP supports and why they are insufficient
answers: Between September 29 and October 28, K.T. was physically aggressive toward peers on seven dated occasions (October 2, 6, 9, 14, 17, 22 and 27)<sup>1</sup>, each lasting 5–15 minutes at moderate intensity and requiring staff de-escalation<sup>1</sup>. Two of these incidents resulted in office referrals<sup>2</sup>. This frequency is unchanged from the 2–3 times per week reported at screening<sup>3</sup>.

K.T. attended weekly outpatient counseling at Piedmont Counseling from January to April 2026, nine sessions<sup>4</sup>. Treatment ended when the family lost transportation. The school's incident count did not decrease during or after that period (four incidents in March, five in April)<sup>2</sup>.

K.T.'s IEP, reviewed March 2026, provides a behaviour plan, preferential seating and a check-in/check-out system<sup>5</sup>. These supports are classroom-based and delivered by school personnel; they do not provide daily clinical intervention or de-escalation during unstructured periods, where five of the seven incidents above occurred<sup>1</sup>. TDT adds licensed clinical oversight and three units of direct intervention per school day, which the IEP cannot provide<sup>3</sup>.

R-0402.early_discharge_text: Units were exhausted ahead of the authorization end date because the client required 3 units per school day throughout (timer log attached: 5 h 10 m average). Need is unchanged: 2 physical incidents and 1 elopement in the last 30 days.

brief.open_with: "This is Jordan Perez, LPC, license and NPI on the request. I'm calling about an eight-year-old girl at an elementary school in Campbell County who was approved for 65 of the 150 units we requested."

criteria.title: Relationships.
criteria.text: Hitting or pushing peers 3× a week in the last 30 days (Oct 1, 3, 8, 10, 15, 17, 22, 24, 28), 5–10 minutes each, needing staff to separate her. 3 office referrals. Classes: 6, passing 3.

criteria.title: Interventions that have not worked.
criteria.text: School counseling weekly since Sep 2025 — ongoing, no change. Outpatient Jan–May 2026, 11 sessions — ended by the provider as "not making progress."

brief.level_of_care: Risk of a more restrictive setting: the school raised an alternative placement at the Oct 14 IEP meeting. Without daily intervention she is likely to be moved.
questions: The IEP gives her a behaviour plan and seating. It gives her no clinical staff at lunch and transitions, where 6 of the 9 incidents happened.
That is not a criterion for TDT. She meets two of the three listed criteria and one level-of-care criterion.
"You can't be spending 5 hours a day."
Staff log start and stop times on their phones. October average: 5 h 12 min a day, including lunch and transitions. I can send the log.
"She's been in services a long time."
Since Feb 2026. Incidents fell from daily to 3× a week; the goal is 1× a week before step-down. Progress is the reason to continue, not to stop.

R-0384.denial_text: Only the guardian can appeal. Drafted for her: a one-page plain-language letter, the reason restated, and what the payer's own letter means — so "approved for less" is not read as "out of danger." Harvest keeps serving in the meantime; that choice is logged with the date.

payer_history.sent: More evidence (suspended, eloped, aggressive) + counter at 140
payer_history.lesson: below the opening offer. More information produced a smaller award.

denial_reasons.check: Current-services table states each service's frequency and why it is insufficient alone — the too-many / too-few catch-22, answered in one field.
IEP status and school-coordination narrative required; what the IEP does and does not provide is named.
Prior-services table: provider, dates, outcome — pro-bono and phantom services flagged as "will not count as evidence of prior care."
PHQ-9 trend, safety-plan reviews and guardian-reported sleep/withdrawal are pulled in as observed data, dated within 30 days.

denial_reasons.reason: "School counseling is not a covered service"
denial_reasons.check: Listed under care coordination rather than as the failed prior service, so it cannot be dismissed.
Draft blocks on an empty outcomes column; asks the guardian question before submission, not after a denial.

denial_reasons.reason: "There's no way you're spending 5+ hours with these kids"
denial_reasons.check: Staff tap start/stop on their phone during the day, so there is a time-stamped record of 3 units a day, including lunch and transitions.
